$comment: Populated from the live public status page at https://status.overleaf.com/ (fetched 2026-09-23). That page is a client-rendered (Next.js) incident.io status page; a plain HTTP fetch returns the current per-component status and the rolling uptime percentage shown on the page, but NOT day-by-day incident history (the calendar view renders client-side and has no public JSON API that was discoverable). So 'history' below is only as deep as what could be confirmed at fetch time (today, no open incidents) plus the rolling window percentage FedRAMP.gov shows on the public page. Before relying on this for the real CDS-TRC Class B requirement, either (a) wire this up to poll https://status.overleaf.com on a schedule and build real daily history, or (b) ask the team running status.overleaf.com (incident.io) whether a machine-readable history export/API is available.
overallStatus: Fully operational — no known issues affecting our systems (as displayed on status.overleaf.com at fetch time).
hostingNote: TODO: this file/page must be served from infrastructure independent of the primary Overleaf service (e.g. a separate static host or CDN) so it stays reachable during an Overleaf outage — this is a firm Class B requirement, not optional. GitHub Pages (used for this starter) satisfies that independence, but a production version should confirm this explicitly.
